questions.text: The business has a written plan for the next 12 months that sets sales and profit targets.
Staff who run sales, production or service can state the current target for their own area.
Before any large spend on equipment, stock or expansion, the owner writes down the cost, the expected extra income and the payback time.
The business has customers who come back to buy again, and the records can show this.
In the last 12 months the business changed a product, service or delivery method because customers told it what they wanted.
The business can say clearly why customers choose it over a competitor, and customers give the same reason when asked.
A written plan says how and where new customers will be found this year.
The business keeps a list of customer names and phone numbers and uses it to reach customers directly.
Share of sales in the last 12 months that came from the single largest customer.
The business knows which way of reaching customers (referral, shop location, WhatsApp, social media, radio, agents) brings the most new customers.
The price of each main product or service is set from its cost plus a target margin.
How often does the owner check competitors' prices and offers?
Discounts and price reductions are given under a rule, not case by case on request.
Orders are delivered on the agreed day and to the agreed specification.
Products or work are checked against a stated standard before they reach the customer.
Customer complaints, returns and refunds are written down and followed up.
The main products or services are made or delivered by following set steps, so different staff produce the same result.
Stock, materials or supplies on hand are physically counted and compared with the stock records.
Each key input or item for resale can be bought from at least two known suppliers.
Waste, spoilage, breakage or loss is measured as a share of what is bought or produced.
Each month the main cost lines (inputs, transport, power, rent, wages) are compared with the previous month and rises are explained.
Equipment and vehicles are serviced on a planned schedule rather than only after they break down.
The business keeps a list of its equipment and other assets with purchase cost, date and condition.
Output or work completed per worker or per day is measured for the main product or service.
The main work process has no regular bottleneck that delays orders.
All cash and mobile money received and paid out is written in a cash book or other record every week.
Business money is kept separate from the owner's household and personal money.
Sales and purchases are recorded in a ledger or software with the date, amount and the customer or supplier.
Receipts, invoices and waybills are filed so that any transaction in the last 12 months can be traced.
Weeks of fixed costs (rent, wages, loan repayments, power, transport) that cash on hand and in accounts could pay today.
A written cash forecast shows the money expected in and out over the coming weeks.
Average number of days customers take to pay on credit sales.
The gross margin (sales less direct cost) is known for each main product or service.
The monthly sales needed to cover all costs (break-even) has been calculated.
Net profit or loss after all costs, including the owner's own pay, has been worked out for the last 12 months.
Financial statements (income statement and balance sheet) have been prepared for the last full year.
Payments above a set limit need approval from someone other than the person asking for the money.
Cash, bank and mobile money balances are reconciled to the business records at least monthly.
All loans and supplier credit are repaid on or before the due date.
Monthly cash available before loan repayments compared with the monthly loan repayments (debt cover).
The business keeps an up to date list of everything it owes (loans, supplier balances, advances) with amounts and due dates.
Borrowed money is used for stock, equipment or other items that earn income, not for routine shortfalls or personal spending.
The business and its owner have no unresolved loan default, court judgement or blacklisting with a lender or credit bureau.
The owner has obtained a copy of their own credit report from a licensed credit bureau and checked it for errors.
The business or owner saves regularly in a bank, susu or VSLA for planned business needs.
The business has prepared and submitted a complete loan, grant or investment application in the last three years.
A written funding plan states how much money is needed, for what, from which source and by when.
The business can show financial projections for the next 12 to 36 months with the assumptions written down.
Who owns the business, and in what shares, is written down and can be shown.
The owner can put together a funder information pack (records, statements and registration documents) within one working day.
The business can run for a week without the owner on site, with sales and daily decisions continuing.
A deputy or successor for the owner's role has been named in writing.
How often does the owner set aside time to work on the business (planning, review, improving), not only in it?
In the last 12 months the owner changed a business practice after training, coaching or advice.
Every person's role and who they report to is written down.
People working in the business (staff, apprentices, helpers) are trained for their jobs when they join and when their tasks change.
People who perform well are recognised or rewarded in a clear and fair way.
The business knows how many people left in the last 12 months and why.
How often does the owner meet staff or the management team to review sales, costs, cash and actions?
Someone outside the business and the owner's family (adviser, mentor, board member) regularly challenges major decisions.
Staff know in writing which decisions they can make without asking the owner (spending, pricing, hiring, discounts).
Employees have a written statement of their job, pay, hours and leave.
Basic safety measures are in place for the main hazards of the work.
Registration certificates, licences, permits, leases, contracts and insurance papers are kept together in one safe place.
Every sale of value is supported by an invoice, receipt or order note that the business keeps a copy of.
The three most important routine tasks (for example cash handling, receiving goods, processing orders) each have written steps.
Someone other than the owner can find and read the main business records.
Share of sales receipts that go through mobile money or a bank account.
The business has a bank account or mobile money business wallet in the business's name that is in regular use.
Sales and accounts are kept in a spreadsheet or software, not only on paper or in the owner's head.
Customers can reach the business through a dedicated business phone number, WhatsApp Business or email address.
The business tracks a small set of numbers every month (sales, gross margin, cash balance, money owed by customers, stock).
In the last six months the owner has made a decision that was clearly based on the recorded figures.
The owner compares this year's results with last year's at least once a year.
At least each quarter, actual results are compared with the plan or budget and the differences are explained in writing.
The business is legally registered and its registration is current (certificate valid, annual renewal or annual return up to date).
All tax returns that fell due in the last 12 months have been filed on time with the Ghana Revenue Authority.
The owner can say which GRA taxes apply to the business (income tax, VAT, PAYE, withholding) and keeps a calendar of due dates.
Employee SSNIT contributions and PAYE are paid by the due date every month.
Important sales and supply arrangements (large customers, key suppliers, premises) are in written agreements.
The business has a right to use its premises for at least the next 12 months, shown in a lease, tenancy agreement or title.
The business has taken a step to stop its brand name, logo or product design being copied.
The owner has written a list of the main risks to the business (fire, theft, price changes, loss of a key customer, illness) and what will be done about each.
The business holds valid insurance for its biggest insurable risks (stock, premises, vehicles, workers).
Valuable stock and cash are protected by physical controls (locks, safe, limited keyholders, cash banked regularly).
Written steps exist for keeping key activities running after a disruption (fire, power cut, illness of a key person, loss of premises).
Business records and customer data are backed up so they could be recovered after loss of a phone, computer or the premises.
The business handles personal data about customers and staff in line with the Data Protection Act, including registration with the Data Protection Commission.
Electricity, fuel and water use and cost are tracked every month.
In the last 12 months the business has taken at least one action to cut energy or water use (LED lighting, solar, efficient equipment, repairing leaks).
Waste (packaging, scrap, used oil, chemicals, electronic waste, organic waste) is sorted, reused or disposed of safely.
The business has taken a practical step against a climate hazard that affects it (flood, heat, drought, storm, power outages).
Women and men doing the same work in the business are paid equally and have the same chance of promotion.
Both women and people under 35 hold jobs with real responsibility (supervisor, technician, manager), not only casual or lowest paid roles.
Women who own, work in or help run the business take part in decisions about how its income is spent.
The workplace has a rule against harassment and a safe way for staff to report it.
The owner has written down what the business would do if monthly sales fell by a quarter for three months.
Share of sales in the last 12 months that came from the largest single product or service line.
The owner belongs to a business association, cooperative, trade group or peer network and has attended its meetings.
At least two people can perform each critical task (taking orders, bookkeeping, production, delivery).
